claims.claim: Clean local main strictly behind configured upstream main fast-forwards before TASK loading and admission during Human-facing PRIMARY launch, binding the synchronized upstream main SHA as RUN base_sha.
When local main is already equal to configured upstream main, pre-admission synchronization is a no-op on committed repository state and PRIMARY admission proceeds normally.

Deterministic fail-closed behavior before RUN creation and before Executor invocation is enforced for dirty worktree, local-ahead, diverged, detached or non-main checkout, missing or ambiguous upstream, and fetch or synchronization failure.

When synchronization advances kernel source/TASK state, direct execution cannot continue under stale pre-sync kernel state and fails closed, while Human-facing launch synchronizes and restarts under synchronized kernel code so the TASK consumed by the RUN is the synchronized canonical TASK.
REMEDIATION, REPAIR, and direct candidate acceptance paths retain their existing exact-HEAD lineage behavior and do not auto-fast-forward to upstream main when upstream is ahead.

Synchronization regressions verify that fast-forward is strictly non-mutating with respect to remote main and uses only read-tree and update-ref without merge, rebase, reset, stash, checkout, clean, pull, push, revert, or conflict resolution.

Existing PRIMARY admission, exactly-one dispatch, Runtime verification, 60/65 timing, interruption terminalization, deterministic model defaults, transport, and failure semantics continue to pass regression coverage.
